title: [clangd][HLSL] Hover produces no tooltip for loop/branch control attributes ([unroll], [loop], [branch], [flatten])
body_truncated:
## Expected behavior

Hovering over `[unroll]`, `[loop]`, `[branch]`, or `[flatten]` should display the attribute name and documentation about its effect on GPU shader execution.

## Observed behavior

Hovering over these attributes produces no tooltip at all. Hovering over declaration attributes like `[numthreads(1,1,1)]` or `[shader("compute")]` works correctly; only statement attributes are affected.

## Reproduction

```hlsl
[numthreads(1, 1, 1)]
void main() {
  [unroll]
  for (int i = 0; i < 4; i++) {
    // ...
  }
}
```

Hovering over `[numthreads(1,1,1)]` shows the expected tooltip. Hovering over `[unroll]` shows nothing.

## Root cause

`[unroll]`/`[loop]`/`[branch]`/`[flatten]` are statement attributes that live inside an `AttributedStmt` node in the AST. clangd's `SelectionTree` (`clang-tools-extra/clangd/Selection.cpp`) has no override for `AttributedStmt`. The base `RecursiveASTVisitor` visits the child statement but does not call `TraverseAttr` for attributes attached to it, so `HLSLLoopHintAttr`/`HLSLControlFlowHintAttr` are invisible to the selection tree, and hover requests never reach them.

Declaration attributes (`[numthreads]`, `[shader]`) work correctly because the `SelectionTree` already traverses attributes via `TraverseAttr` when visiting `FunctionDecl`, `VarDecl`, etc., so the gap is specific to statement attributes.

Note: there's an open upstream PR [#117692](https://github.com/llvm/llvm-project/pull/117692) attempting to fix this generically in `RecursiveASTVisitor` itself, unmerged since November 2024 because it also causes the visitor to traverse into attribute *arguments*, which broke `[[clang::nonblocking]]`/`[[clang::nonallocating]]` analysis. Given that, this issue is scoped to a clangd-local fix rather than the base visitor.

## Proposed fix

Extend clangd's `SelectionTree` to traverse attributes attached to `AttributedStmt` nodes before visiting the underlying statement (i.e. override `TraverseAttributedStmt` in `SelectionVisitor

title: [clangd][HLSL] register hover not triggered when cursor is inside the argument
body_truncated:
## Expected behavior

Hovering on the slot identifier inside `register(t1)` (e.g. on `t1`) should display the
register documentation, including a description of what `t` means (SRV).

## Observed behavior

Hovering inside the argument produces no tooltip, only hovering on the `register` keyword
itself works.

## Reproduction

```hlsl
Texture2D tex : register(t1);
```

Hovering on `register` shows the expected documentation. Hovering on `t1` (inside the
parentheses) shows nothing.

## Root cause

`ParseHLSLAnnotations` (`clang/lib/Parse/ParseHLSL.cpp`) captures a single `SourceLocation
Loc` right after consuming the `register`/annotation token, and this is the only location
passed to `Attrs.addNew`:

```cpp
Attrs.addNew(II, Loc, AttributeScopeInfo(), ArgExprs.data(), ArgExprs.size(),
             ParsedAttr::Form::HLSLAnnotation());
```

No `SourceRange` spanning the full `register(...)` construct (including its closing `)`) is
ever captured or passed, so the resulting attribute has an effectively zero-width range. When
clangd's `SelectionTree` checks whether the cursor falls inside an attribute, a zero-width
range never matches, so hover requests inside the argument never reach the attribute.

## Proposed fix

Inside the `AT_HLSLResourceBinding` case, capture the closing `)` location before it's
consumed by `ExpectAndConsume(tok::r_paren, ...)`, and thread a full `SourceRange` (from the
attribute start to the closing paren) into `Attrs.addNew` instead of the single
`SourceLocation`.

title: [clangd][HLSL] Hover produces no information for vector swizzle and matrix element access
Factor out mergeFixits() logic from DiagnosticRenderer and reuse it in clangd
body_truncated:
While investigating https://github.com/llvm/llvm-project/issues/185108, we discovered that clang-tidy fixits go through a post-processing step called [mergeFixits()](https://searchfox.org/llvm/rev/4fb7bf3323ea54d929f3846e6cd28d9dda1b891c/clang/lib/Frontend/DiagnosticRenderer.cpp#104) in `DiagnosticRenderer`, and in some cases this logic can be important for correctness (for example, it involves [adding a space](https://searchfox.org/llvm/rev/4fb7bf3323ea54d929f3846e6cd28d9dda1b891c/clang/lib/Edit/EditedSource.cpp#376-377) if a removal would otherwise result in two tokens being merged).

Clangd also surfaces clang-tidy diagnostics and applies their fixits, but does not use `DiagnosticRenderer`, and so does not benefit from this post-processing logic.

A class called "renderer" is probably not the best place to have logic that's important for the correctness of applying a fixit. This issue tracks factoring out the `mergeFixits()` logic from `DiagnosticRenderer`, and using it in clangd as well.

title: [clangd] Allow indexing of exposed resource directory headers

Most of these are intended to be present in user code, however they prefer to use reserved keywords as they are commonly a part of system headers. These functions are not indexed, which makes working with them very difficult. title: clangd in MSVC mode crashes when indexing a C source file which defines assert macro
body_truncated:
In MSVC compat mode, a simple C source code like this causes clangd to make an illegal hash map insertion, leading to a crash that can be observed with an assertions enabled build:
```
#define assert
```
Produces:
```
Assertion failed: !KeyInfoT::isEqual(Val, EmptyKey) && !KeyInfoT::isEqual(Val, TombstoneKey) && "Empty/Tombstone value shouldn't be inserted into map!"
```

The problem here is that we are not checking for invalid source locations when inserting symbols into the symbol -> include file map, which is a situation that occurs with synthesized symbols.

In this repro, the assert definition triggers a workaround (https://github.com/llvm/llvm-project/commit/8da090381d567d0ec555840f6b2a651d2997e4b3) where a `static_assert` macro is also implicitly defined.

title: clangd 15 regressed performance of parsing long headers
body_truncated:
The 15 address introduced a bug where we accidentally scan up to the end of source files every time we see a comment: https://reviews.llvm.org/D135314 has details

Some users/codebases are seeing a large performance regression due to this. See https://github.com/clangd/clangd/issues/1316

It has a simple fix, we should backport it.
